scope: Original20: Sol User/Semi RTT S and H; Opus User Static H. Offline review of saved evidence against each judgment's original rubric.
decisions: The code produces a linkage tree, memberships and within-cluster summaries, but never uses a cluster ordering to reorder both axes of the correlation matrix. This explicit A requirement is absent; retain partial clustering credit. Apply the same correction to selected and heldout A ratings.

The code verifies distance symmetry and saves cluster membership, but does not reorder correlation-matrix rows and columns by the hierarchy. Distance symmetry is not the required symmetric matrix reordering. The otherwise valid documented clustering merits B.

The linkage/fcluster code prints memberships without a clustered matrix ordering. The selected reason's claim that a shared ordering was used is not supported by the saved code; award B for partial implementation.

The saved linkage and cluster-membership workflow has no symmetric row/column reordering of the correlation matrix, an explicit full-credit requirement. Correct both selected and heldout A ratings, preserving their existing B counterparts.

The workflow creates linkage, cluster labels and cut sensitivities but no clustered matrix reordering. All four original clauses require reordering both axes; apply B to S and every H, rather than lowering only S.

Counts and frequencies for naive/post-treatment groups are reported, but the only reported Fisher p-value is the MAPK-by-ESR1 comparison. It cannot also satisfy the explicitly required naive-versus-post-therapy p-value. Partial reporting warrants B in both selected and heldout.

The 56/735 versus 88/687 comparison has no p-value. The reported p=4.7456576e-06 instead tests ESR1 versus MAPK status. The full-credit clause requires both comparisons; retain B for the substantial but incomplete reporting.

The only contingency test is ESR1-mutated versus wild-type MAPK prevalence; no naive-versus-post-therapy p-value accompanies 50/660 versus 103/727. Correct all A ratings for this reporting omission, retaining existing B ratings.

The selected reason awards full reporting credit for counts and frequencies alone. The saved report provides an ESR1 association p-value and a separate gene-pair screen, but no naive-versus-post-therapy p-value required by A. B is the original rubric's incomplete-reporting level.

The cohort filter explicitly includes ALS-AD and ALS-FTD along with ALS, rather than disease == ALS required for A. The selected reason acknowledges this deviation but still assigns A. Partial cohort-definition credit B is appropriate; this is not absence of a valid cohort.

Both endpoints are correctly ranked by absolute estimate and five leading proteins per endpoint have signed estimates and adjusted p-values. In these two original clauses, top 10 and the listed proteins are examples, not mandatory cardinality. Do not add that requirement. Variant 2 explicitly requires top 10 and remains B; showing code that could print 15 is not treated as proof that 15 values were reported.

The fold-change vectors give F ratios 0.927634 and 0.884998 for curated/human self-assembly, yet the conclusion calls this strong F enrichment. Full credit requires correct above/below-one interpretation. Retain partial credit for correctly computed ratios; do not label the whole calculation absent.

Human/curated frequency calculations are present, but their explicit claimed F-enrichment concordance reverses the meaning of both ratios below one. The required accurate cross-dataset pattern comparison is not fully met; award partial replication credit.

The report gives available predictor AUCs and task comparisons, but never references the random-classifier AUC=0.5 baseline. The original B clause explicitly lists omission of that baseline; unavailable FuzDrop is not the reason for this correction.

BH adjustment is implemented, but the answer and results table mix incompatible p/FDR sets: the purported authoritative output has minimum FDR 0.205, while the report also calls two pathways significant with FDR 1.43e-6 and 0.00460. Full-credit consistent application/reporting is not supported. Keep partial credit for the actual BH procedure.

Discordant examples/counts are present, but no biological explanation for why they disagree is supplied. Full credit requires a biological rationale for discordance, not merely named proteins and opposite signs. Existing partial-credit variants remain unchanged.

The report names and groups discordant proteins but gives no regimen/mechanistic explanation for their discordance; it explicitly limits labels to descriptive groupings. B explicitly covers discordants with superficial or absent explanation. No additional database lookup requirement is imposed.

Concordance, regimen differences and limitations are reported, but the required biological account involving estrogen/reduced androgens and an explanation of SPIRO/CPA differences is absent. Retain B for correct but limited interpretation; caution about causality is not penalized.

The hierarchy, symmetric distance and membership validation are present, but no symmetric reordering of correlation-matrix rows/columns is performed. This is the same missing explicit A requirement found in the RTT review; preserve partial clustering credit.

QC/PCA and continuous-covariate residualization are present, but the actual site/platform/library-preparation batch variables are explicitly not corrected. Disclosure does not satisfy the full-credit batch-correction requirement; retain partial credit for the completed preprocessing.

The trace expressly says the reported top-list values came from an earlier unweighted approximation and cannot be claimed to match the corrected weighted script. The ranked lists exist, but full accuracy for the claimed analysis is not established; keep B rather than A.

The reported Fisher p-value tests ESR1/MAPK association. There is no p-value for the naive-versus-post-treatment prevalence comparison, which the full-credit reporting clause separately requires. Keep counts/frequencies as partial reporting credit.

The saved input audit explicitly finds all four BAMs absent. Auditing their expected paths is not loading the matching BAMs, as A requires. The correctly mapped peak inputs support B rather than no cohort credit.

The answer explicitly leaves global accessibility unresolved and distinguishes peak-call contraction from an accessibility conclusion. B requires a directional conclusion; C explicitly covers no clear global conclusion. Mechanistic-context and limitations credit are not changed.

The answer says the quantitative question cannot be resolved and explicitly says fewer peaks are not an answer. This is not the directional global conclusion required for B; apply C's no-clear-conclusion clause, preserving separate partial-method and interpretation credit.

retained.da-15-2-user-r2/S/criterion_3: The scale-free-fit proxy uses gene row indices and eigengenes are approximated by means, but adjacency/TOM/module detection are genuinely present. The B-versus-C boundary is not sufficiently unambiguous for a further manual downgrade; retain B and record the implementation weakness.
retained.da-10-1-static-r2/criterion_5: The displayed vectors are alphabetical, but the code explicitly constructs and applies the same IDR-frequency order across four comparisons. This does not establish absence of property-based organization; retain.
retained.da-19-6-static/criterion_2: B explicitly permits region-level presence/absence as partial work. Do not downgrade every incomplete read-coverage workflow solely for missing BAMs; conclusion and input-loading criteria are assessed separately.
retained.other_machine_means: No matching per-artifact judgments from the other machine were supplied. Neither 80.5 nor the 0.6–0.8 interval is used in correction selection or computation.
retained.other_disagreements: Cross-auditor agreement, selected A, target-number mismatches, and interpretive strictness alone are not sufficient evidence to alter a rating. Previously supported 59 corrections remain in effect.
